assessment.documented_product_goal: A multilingual tourist mobile audio-guide application with location discovery, approved multilingual guide delivery and playback, offline content management, geofence notifications, plus web administration for content and analytics/feedback.

use_case_inventory.name: Explore & Select location
use_case_inventory.scope: Location discovery and selection via nearby GPS, keyword, map, or category; ends at Location Details.

use_case_inventory.name: Access Multilingual Guide Content
use_case_inventory.scope: Load only approved script text for selected location/language/FULL or SHORT mode, including EN then VI fallback.

use_case_inventory.name: Play Audio Guide
use_case_inventory.scope: Play matching audio or fall back to device TTS, with playback controls and audio-focus handling.

use_case_inventory.name: Manage & Update Offline Content
use_case_inventory.scope: Check, download, verify, replace, resume, or delete optional offline content while protecting bundled base content.

use_case_inventory.name: Receive Location-Based Notifications
use_case_inventory.scope: Detect geofence entry, enforce cooldown, display notification/banner, and route selection to Location Details.

use_case_inventory.name: Manage Location Content & Audio Assets
use_case_inventory.scope: Create/edit location, scripts, and audio; save only DRAFT or PENDING_REVIEW.

use_case_inventory.name: System Analytics & Tourist Feedback Management
use_case_inventory.scope: View usage metrics, inspect/filter/update feedback status, and export the current report.

workflow_dependencies: UC-01 supplies locationId to UC-02; UC-02 supplies locationId, languageCode, scriptType, and scriptText to UC-03.
UC-04 supplies/version-controls offline data used by UC-02 and UC-03.
UC-05 routes to Location Details; its stated MVP boundary delegates guide loading/playback to UC-02/UC-03.
UC-06 creates DRAFT/PENDING_REVIEW content; UC-02 exposes APPROVED content only.

scope_assessment.mvp_fit: The seven use cases cover a coherent tourist journey and the minimum administration needed to maintain it. UC-04 and UC-07 each combine related operational actions, but the document explicitly treats their variants as behaviors inside one use case, which is reasonable for the stated MVP.
scope_assessment.overlap: UC-01/UC-05 both lead to Location Details but have distinct triggers (manual discovery versus geofence event). UC-02/UC-03 are appropriately separated as content retrieval versus playback. UC-06 and UC-07 have distinct admin goals and actors.
scope_assessment.extension_points: Every use case records Extension Points as N/A. Cross-use-case handoffs are documented in triggers, preconditions, assumptions, and rules instead of formal extension points.

findings.title: UC-05's playback relationship conflicts with its own MVP boundary
findings.evidence: UC-03 says that UC-05 may trigger UC-03 when a tourist enters a configured area, and the UC3 draw.io note says 'manual or triggered by UC-05'. UC-05's assumptions instead state that selecting a notification only opens Location Details and that loading/playback remain responsibilities of UC-02 and UC-03.
findings.impact: The documented geofence experience is ambiguous: it could auto-play audio on entry, or merely open Location Details after the tourist selects a notification. These paths have materially different consent, audio-focus, and notification behavior.
findings.recommendation: Choose one documented MVP behavior and align UC-03 trigger, UC-05 basic/alternative paths, assumptions, and the UC3 diagram. If automatic playback is intentionally deferred, remove the UC-05-to-UC-03 trigger rather than leaving it as an implied extension.

findings.title: The content lifecycle stops at PENDING_REVIEW while tourist delivery requires APPROVED
findings.evidence: UC-06 can save only DRAFT or PENDING_REVIEW and explicitly puts approval, publishing, and Mobile App synchronization outside its scope. UC-02 permits only status=APPROVED content.
findings.impact: The documented use-case set does not trace how admin-authored content becomes eligible for tourist retrieval, nor how an approved revision reaches mobile/offline data.
findings.recommendation: Record the approval/publishing/synchronization function as a separate out-of-scope dependency or a future use case, with its ownership and handoff to UC-02/UC-04. Do not imply it is performed by UC-06.

findings.title: Offline-content assumptions differ on whether prior download is needed
findings.evidence: UC-01 assumes that offline use requires a previously downloaded package containing the SQLite database. UC-04 states that base offline content is bundled with the application, allowing UC-02 and UC-03 to operate offline without any prior download.
findings.impact: The minimum offline installation state is unclear, which affects onboarding, storage expectations, and the availability of nearby-location discovery.
findings.recommendation: State one baseline explicitly: whether the bundled base package includes the location database required by UC-01, and distinguish it from optional downloaded updates/assets.

findings.title: Tourist feedback creation is an external dependency with no documented owner
findings.evidence: UC-07 assumes feedback has already been stored and says the tourist feedback form is defined elsewhere; the PRD use-case inventory contains no use case for submitting that feedback.
findings.impact: Analytics/feedback management can be specified, but the source, validation, and lifecycle entry point of the feedback data are not traceable within this documented scope.
findings.recommendation: Name the external feedback-submission function/system and its handoff to UC-07, or add it as a separately scoped future use case if it belongs to this product.

findings.title: Use-case numbering in basic flows is global rather than locally reset
findings.evidence: UC-01 basic flow starts at 1, UC-02 starts at 7, and UC-03 starts at 12, while UC-04 through UC-07 reset to 1.
findings.impact: References to numbered steps are less easy to review and maintain because the convention changes across use cases.
findings.recommendation: Reset basic-flow numbering within each use case and update any step references in alternatives/exceptions accordingly.
source_evidence: PRD UC-01 to UC-03 Basic Course of Event

documented_strengths: Each use case identifies an actor, goal, trigger, precondition, postcondition, alternatives/exceptions, assumptions, and business rules.
The tourist flow has explicit, resilient fallbacks: manual discovery after GPS denial, language fallback, TTS after audio failure, and safe offline-update recovery.
Business rules protect key integrity boundaries: approved-only content, matching content identifiers, verified updates, cooldown/locationId routing, and draft/pending-review status controls.
The draw.io file contains UC1 through UC7 and activity diagrams, supporting the stated PRD workflows.
overall_conclusion: The PRD defines a coherent and mostly MVP-sized set of tourist and administrative use cases. The primary documentation risks are the unresolved geofence-to-playback behavior, the untraced approval/publication lifecycle, and conflicting offline baseline assumptions; resolving those boundaries would make the use-case model implementation-ready without expanding the product scope.
